topic: Introduction to Civil Engineering and Its Branches
title: Civil Engineering Branches Explained Simply | Civil Engineering Ep 1
description:
In Hosahalli, the old government school leaks every monsoon, and now a crack runs over a classroom door. The town will build a new two-storey school for 600 children, and this series follows that one building from the empty plot to handover day. In Episode 1 we meet the team: Ananya, the young site engineer, Raghu the head mason, Farhan the surveyor, Prof. Deshpande the design checker, and Mrs. Lakshmi, the headmistress who asks the only question that matters: will my children be safe?

You will see Thomas Tredgold's 1828 definition of civil engineering, used for the Royal Charter of the Institution of Civil Engineers, and then watch the new school built up on one drawing, branch by branch: surveying pegs the levels, geotechnical engineering drills a borehole and sizes the footings, structural engineering adds columns, beams and slabs and sends the load down to the ground, water and environmental engineering add a tank, pipes and drains, transportation plans the road and bus bay, and construction management turns it all into a schedule. Then we meet all seven main branches and see four of them at work today, in a city hospital, a metro line, a water board and a highway project. We also look at the human side honestly: safe homes, clean water and roads on one side; cost, delays and failures that hurt people on the other. And we remember Engineers' Day in India, 15 September, the birthday of Sir M. Visvesvaraya.

This is Episode 1 of our Civil Engineering series for B.E. and B.Tech Civil students.
